subtype: Approach: friends make a plan and nobody questions the risks [Pitfall]
passage:
The plan came together in the canteen on Friday: five friends, a waterfall trail, Saturday afternoon, back by dark. Nobody mentioned that the bus left late or that the sky over the hills was already heavy.
Dhruv looked at the clouds and thought about wet rocks. Asif thought about the walk back in the dark. Each glanced round the table, everyone else was smiling, and each said nothing. "Great plan," someone said, and they clapped.
At the trailhead at four, thunder rolled in. The tea-stall owner shook his head. "The path shuts before dusk, and rain is coming."
They stood in silence until Asif said, "I was worried the whole way." "Me too," said Dhruv, and the others nodded. Dhruv called his father, and they waited under the stall's roof until he came. The fare was spent and nobody saw the waterfall.

qa.a: The plan came together in the canteen on Friday.

qa.q: What was Asif worried about while the group clapped?
qa.a: Asif was worried and uneasy about the walk back in the dark, and said nothing because everyone else was smiling.

qa.q: What could the friends have done at the canteen table?
qa.a: Any one of them could have said the worry aloud and suggested going earlier or another day, since several shared the same fear.

qa.q: How might the tea-stall owner see the group?
qa.a: The owner shook their head and warned about the path shutting before dusk, so probably sees a group who set out too late.

grounding: Friends plan a late waterfall trip and each privately worries about safety but assumes the rest are fine, so nobody questions the risks.

subtype: Approach: friends make a plan and nobody questions the risks [Pitfall]
passage: Uma, Charu and three friends had planned it all in the class group: a Saturday trip to the waterfall outside Pune, leaving after tuition at four. Uma looked at the map. It would be dark by the time they reached the rocks. She wanted to say something, but everyone was sending excited stickers. "They must think it's fine," she told herself. Charu was thinking the same. So was at least one other. Nobody said it. On Saturday they reached the falls at 6:15. The path was slippery, the light was fading, and Charu scraped her knee on the rocks. Uma finally said, "I didn't want to come this late." Charu stared. "Neither did I." They phoned Uma's father, walked back to the road together, and he picked them up.

qa.q: What time did they reach the falls?
What was Uma feeling when everyone sent stickers?
qa.a: She felt worried about the dark and slippery rocks, but uneasy about being the only one to speak up.

qa.q: What could the group have done differently in the planning chat?
qa.a: Someone could have asked, "Is everyone okay with reaching after dark?" so private worries came out before the trip.

qa.q: How does Charu feel when Uma finally speaks?
qa.a: Charu is surprised and relieved, realising she wasn't the only one who was worried.

grounding: Friends plan a late waterfall trip; each privately worries about safety but assumes the others are fine with it.

subtype: Approach: friends make a plan and nobody questions the risks [Pitfall]
passage:
"So, waterfall on Sunday? We leave at five!"
"Five in the evening, Sahil?"
"Yeah, Kavitha. Sunset at the falls. Everyone's in."
"Everyone's in?"
"All six said yes on the group."
Later, by the lake at the falls, as the sky turned grey:
"Sahil, the rocks are really slippery."
"I know. And there's no signal here."
"Why did you plan it so late?"
"Why didn't you say anything? You all said yes."
"I thought you were all fine with it."
"I was scared about the dark from the start."
"So was I!" said Kavitha. "And two of the others said the same thing just now."
Sahil looked at the path, already dim. "Okay. We walk back together, now, before it's darker, and I call Papa to meet us at the road."

qa.q: How many said yes on the group?
qa.a: All six said yes on the group.

qa.q: What does Sahil's admission 'I was scared about the dark from the start' reveal?
qa.a: It reveals Sahil was anxious all along but stayed quiet, assuming everyone else was comfortable.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could fix it next time?
qa.a: Everyone hid their worry and assumed others were fine; one honest question in the group before the trip would have changed the plan.

qa.q: How might Sahil's father feel getting the call?
qa.a: He may feel worried but relieved that they called and are coming back together before dark.

grounding: Friends plan a late waterfall trip; each privately worries about safety but assumes the others are fine.
